fullPassage: Based on discoveries in neuroscience, pain and pleasure are formed and processed in the same area of the brain. Our bodies constantly strive for homeostasis, which is defined as the balance of bodily functions. Without the body's effective compensatory mechanisms, which may cushion potential highs and lows, we would not be capable of surviving. Pleasure and pain are like two sides of the same coin; they seem to work together and are heavily reliant on one another and keep balance. If you imagine pleasure and pain as the two opposite points on a scale, you can easily understand that as one of the two points rises, the other must correspondingly fall. We've all heard the expression, "No pain, no gain." Well, according to psychiatrist Dr. Anna Lembke, there may be some truth to these words. She says that our attempts to escape being miserable are in fact making us even more miserable. This is because pain is actually an essential component of our ability to maintain a neutral state, and allowing it will in turn reset our internal scale back to balance.

❌ ② supplement — 보충제 (첨가물 뉘앙스)
❌ ③ instrument — 도구, 기구 (부분이 아닌 독립적 도구)
✅ ④ component — 구성요소 ←정답
det.tip: component = 구성요소, 부품 (a part of a larger whole)

questions.passage: Our bodies constantly strive for homeostasis, which is __________ (define) as the balance of bodily functions.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 항상성은 신체 기능의 균형으로 '정의된다' → 과거분사 defined (수동태 is defined)
det.analysis: which is __________ as → 수동태 자리. define(정의하다) → defined(정의된)로 변환. be defined as = ~으로 정의되다
det.tip: define(정의하다) → defined(과거분사, 수동태: is defined as)

questions.passage: This is because pain is actually an essential component of our ability to maintain a neutral state, and __________ (allow) it will in turn reset our internal scale back to balance.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 고통을 '허용하면' 결국 내부 저울이 균형으로 재설정된다 → 동명사 allowing (주어 역할)
det.analysis: __________ it will in turn reset → 주어 자리. allow(허용하다) → allowing(동명사)으로 변환. allowing it = 그것을 허용하는 것이
det.tip: allow(허용하다) → allowing(동명사, 주어: allowing it will...)

questions.passage: Based on discoveries in neuroscience, pain and pleasure are formed and processed in the same area of the brain. Our bodies constantly strive for homeostasis, which is defined as the balance of bodily functions. Without the body's effective compensatory mechanisms, which may cushion potential highs and lows, we would not be capable of surviving. Pleasure and pain are like __________; they seem to work together and are heavily reliant on one another and keep balance. If you imagine pleasure and pain as the two opposite points on a scale, you can easily understand that as one of the two points rises, the other must correspondingly fall. We've all heard the expression, "No pain, no gain." Well, according to psychiatrist Dr. Anna Lembke, there may be some truth to these words. She says that our attempts to escape being miserable are in fact making us even more miserable. This is because pain is actually an essential component of our ability to maintain a neutral state, and allowing it will in turn reset our internal scale back to balance.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 쾌락과 고통은 '동전의 양면'과 같아서 함께 작용하고 서로 의존적이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① discovered in the same area — 같은 영역에서 발견된 (앞 문장과 중복, 비유가 아님)
❌ ② opposite points on a scale — 저울 위 반대 지점 (뒤 문장 내용이지 이 자리의 비유가 아님)
✅ ③ two sides of the same coin — 동전의 양면. 뒤에 'work together and are heavily reliant'과 연결 ←정답
❌ ④ essential components of pleasure — 쾌락의 필수 요소 (고통이 쾌락의 요소라는 것은 부정확)
det.tip: two sides of the same coin = 동전의 양면 (불가분의 관계)

ch: two sides of the same coin

questions.passage: Based on discoveries in neuroscience, pain and pleasure are formed and processed in the same area of the brain. Our bodies constantly strive for homeostasis, which is defined as the balance of bodily functions. Without the body's effective compensatory mechanisms, which may cushion potential highs and lows, we would not be capable of surviving. Pleasure and pain are like two sides of the same coin; they seem to work together and are heavily reliant on one another and keep balance. If you imagine pleasure and pain as the two opposite points on a scale, you can easily understand that as one of the two points rises, the other must correspondingly fall. We've all heard the expression, "No pain, no gain." Well, according to psychiatrist Dr. Anna Lembke, there may be some truth to these words. She says that our attempts to escape being miserable are in fact making us even more miserable. This is because pain is actually an essential component of our ability to maintain a neutral state, and __________ our internal scale back to balance.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 고통은 중립 상태 유지의 필수 요소이며, 그것을 '허용하면 결국 내부 저울을 다시 균형으로 되돌린다.'
det.analysis:
❌ ① cushion potential highs and lows — 잠재적 고저를 완충하다 (보상 메커니즘의 역할이지 고통의 효과가 아님)
✅ ② allowing it will in turn reset — 허용하면 결국 재설정한다. 원문과 일치 ←정답
❌ ③ the balance of bodily functions — 신체 기능의 균형 (항상성의 정의이지 고통 허용의 결과가 아님)
❌ ④ escape being miserable and gain — 비참함에서 벗어나 얻다 (오히려 더 비참해진다는 본문과 모순)
det.tip: allowing(허용하는 것) + in turn(결국) + reset(재설정하다) — 고통 허용이 균형 회복의 열쇠

ch: allowing it will in turn reset
